options: A logical grouping of activities that together perform one unit of work
A single data-copy operation only
A connection definition to a data store
A scheduled trigger with no activities attached
questions.explain: A pipeline groups activities so they can be managed, deployed, and scheduled together, rather than one at a time.

questions.q: What are the three groupings every Data Factory activity falls into?
options: Data movement, data transformation, and control
Source, sink, and trigger
Import, export, and delete
Pipeline, dataset, and linked service
questions.explain: Every activity is a data movement activity (like Copy), a data transformation activity (like Data Flow or Stored Procedure), or a control activity (like If Condition or ForEach).

questions.q: Where do you create a new pipeline in Data Factory Studio?
options: The Author hub, select the + icon, then Pipeline
The Monitor hub
The Home page's Configure SSIS tile
Pipelines can only be created through PowerShell
questions.explain: Author hub → + icon → Pipeline → Pipeline opens the pipeline editor, ready to build.

questions.q: What does the pipeline editor's Properties pane control?
options: The pipeline's own name, description, and annotations
Which activities are available to drag onto the canvas
The parameters and variables for whatever activity is selected
The list of every trigger in the data factory
questions.explain: Properties holds the pipeline's own metadata — name, description, annotations — separate from the Activities pane and the configuration pane.

questions.q: What is the default soft limit on activities per pipeline?
options: 120 activities, including those nested inside containers
10 activities total
There is no limit at all
5 activities per pipeline
questions.explain: 120 is generous for nearly any real pipeline. Hitting it is usually a sign to split the work into smaller pipelines chained with an Execute Pipeline activity.
